 INTERVENOR MONROE MOORE RESPONSE TO ONCOR AND LCRA'S OBJECTIONS TO CERTAIN
        INTERVENORS' EXHIBITS LISTED IN ATTACHMENT A OF SOAH ORDER NO. 30
                            Monroe Moore #172 - Intervenor - Docket 59475


Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (together,
"Applicants") filed objections to Intervenor Monroe Moore exhibits listed in Attachment A to
SOAH Order No. 30. Monroe Moore (Intervenor No. 173) submits this response in support of
admitting its exhibits into evidence at the outset of the hearing on the merits. Contrary to the
Applicants' arguments, Monroe Moore Exhibits 1-A – 7-A were included with Monroe Moore
Direct Testimony filed on the Interchange. The exhibits should be admitted into evidence as
part of Monroe Moore Direct Testimony. Exhibits are published by experts in their fields or
are educational material provided to the public by Texas agency and are supporting my direct
testimony. Other items included are photos of the land/property in question.

Exhibit 1 – A titled An Investigation into the Recharge Pathways and Mechanisms in the Northern Segment of the
Edwards Aquifer, Bell County, Texas. Authors: Stephanie S. Wong, graduate student, Dr. Joe C. Yelderman Jr., Ph.D.,
P.G., Baylor University, Department of Geology. This study is supported by Clearwater and focuses on Aquifer health in
Salado Texas supplying our lands only water source. Project overview “A body of research was undertaken by Baylor
University (“Baylor”) to gain a deeper understanding of the Northern Segment of the Edwards Balcones Fault
Zone (BFZ) Aquifer (“the Northern Segment”). Specifically, knowledge of how much recharge occurs and the pathways
that recharge takes to the aquifer will greatly assist groundwater resource management.



                                                                                                                         1
 Exhibit 1 – B Titled Salado Salamander Monitoring Final Report 2025. Authors: Peter H. Diaz Texas Fish and Wildlife
Conservation Office San Marcos Texas, Jennifer Bronson Warren Texas Parks and Wildlife Department Waco Texas,
Justin Crow San Marcos Aquatic Resource Center San Marcos Texas. Study focuses on the health of the Salado
Salamander population located in Salado springs and Aquifers. Executive Summary: Monitoring of the Salado
salamander (Eurycea chisholmensis) concluded in December of 2025 finalizing the 11th year of monitoring at the Salado
Downtown Spring Complex (DSC) and at Robertson Springs in Bell County (Figure 2).

Exhibit 2 – A Title Golden-cheeked Warbler Endangered, distributed by Texas Parks and Wildlife Department Wildlife
Diversity Branch & U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Ecological Services Field Office. This exhibit talks about endangered
wildlife and Texas conservation acts. Federal Status: Endangered, 5/4/90.


Exhibit 2 – B Titled Management Guidelines for the Golden-cheeked Warbler in Rural Landscapes. Funds for the
production of this leaflet were provided by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, under Section 6 of the Endangered Species
Act. This exhibit provides insight into ideal habitats for these endangered species.


Exhibit 2 – C Titled Counties that contain golden-cheeked warbler and Black-Capped Vireo Habitat distributed by Texas
Department of Transpiration. Exhibit shows the proven habitat of this endangered species.


Exhibit 3 – A titled Effect of High-voltage Electrical Field Exposure on Neurobiological Factors and Visual Working
Memory of Macaques, Author Hamed Aliyari, PhD. Address: Department of Psychiatry, University of Texas
Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, Texas. Published in the Basic & Clinical Neuroscience 2025 – vol 16 Special issue.



Exhibit 4 – A           Photo of property - Heritage Live oak - details on location and what in indicated in photo
Exhibit 4 – B           Photo of property – Spring / Creek - details on location and what in indicated in photo
Exhibit 4 – C           Photo of property – Heritage Live oak - details on location and what in indicated in photo
Exhibit 4 – D           Photo of property – Heritage Live oak - details on location and what in indicated in photo
Exhibit 4 – E           Photo of property - Historic photos - details on location and what in indicated in photo


Exhibit 5 – A Copy of Email to Mr. McConnell that was never responded to, about inaccurate information about my land.

To conclude, all exhibits should be admitted into evidence as part of Monroe Moore Direct Testimony.


Respectfully submitted,
Monroe Moore
RESPONSE TO ONCOR AND LCRA'S OBJECTIONS TO EVIDENCE


Date: June 7,2026
